analysis.title: Weekly Mash (Mark Wilson, 6 Nov 2026)
key_insights: Thursday 5 Nov was the first big post-midterm session: VIX's volatility (vol of VIX) had its 2nd largest 1-day move ever, the largest number of US index puts ever traded, and the S&P moved about 4 standard deviations. Wilson calls it a '4.9 sigma event in Nasdaq'.

GS's Dems/Reps policy pair had priced persistently higher midterm risk since early summer. Wilson says the market's usual Trump-era policy playbook may not apply because this time the policy impetus is Democratic, which may need a different reaction function.

Market structure amplified the move: over half of stocks are passively owned, much of daily volume is price-agnostic (quant, systematic, index rebalancing, ETF/factor flows), and the fastest fundamental managers run leveraged books on similar risk models. Moves that standard sigma distributions call improbable become likely on a shrinking denominator.

Correlations have been breaking: Apple is now negatively correlated with the Nasdaq, and the S&P 500 has only a 60% correlation to the equal-weight S&P 500. NVDA realised 100 vol over 5 days, and semis had a historic 5-day drawdown.
GS estimates of Thursday client performance: Fundamental TMT funds -4% on the day, Multi-Strats -140bps.

Credit barely moved on Thursday. The generic 30y credit spread widened only 2.2bps while SPX fell 4.4% (regression implied 8.2bps). GS credit strategists (Reid Zhou) say credit's downside convexity 'hasn't kicked in...yet'.
GS credit strategy pair idea: short the generic IG 30Y basket on swap (rates hedged) versus long SPX future, beta weighted. It exploits the low credit-equity beta and keeps liquidity.

The post-midterm sell-off was entirely in AI spending beneficiaries. The 72 S&P 500 AI infrastructure companies (semis, power, networking, cooling) fell 13.3% over two days, while the 5 hyperscalers rose 1.7% and the rest of the S&P was flat. The S&P is down 2.8% since the election.

AI spending beneficiaries now trade at 13.1x next-12-month earnings, a 26% discount to the S&P 500's 17.8x, the lowest relative and absolute levels since late 2022. Their NTM EPS estimates are up more than 50% relative to the S&P's.

The hi-beta momentum factor has had a >30% 4-week drawdown, is down 15% YTD and is 50%+ off its Q2 high. Monthly return dispersion between SPX-ex-AI and SPX has widened. 10yr UST yields have also traded as an AI trade.

Wilson expects AI to take a less prominent role after the selloff and expects volatility to fall as exposures shrink, so NVDA should not realise 100 vol again over the next 5 days. GS principal components work shows meaningful growth de-rating and policy tightening already priced.

Since July the market has faced slowing second-derivative AI spending, slowing second-derivative earnings growth, higher cost of capital and energy-driven inflation pressure. Wilson sees a meaningful break lower in yields and energy prices. European defensives just had their best month versus EuroStoxx on record, but consumer and rate-sensitive areas have not yet reversed.

Wilson's 25 Sept view was that stagflation is expected but goldilocks (slowing growth, falling inflation, less hawkish central banks) is delivered, which favours equities after a year of de-rating. He says he is still in the 1997/1998 camp, not 1999/2000.
His supports for the bull case: robust payrolls, positioning already hit hard, rates and oil easing, and newly elected Democrats unlikely to want to threaten aggregate growth.

Mega-cap tech (hyperscalers) rose versus broad AI and the NDX and regained half of the ground lost versus the S&P in the prior 3 weeks. The market read the policy as crimping capex, which would help pricing for constrained compute and favour holders of capacity.

Hyperscaler bond issuance was $67b in the last week across 5 deals, taking YTD issuance to $296b, almost $50b above GS's assumption for this calendar year. GS has not yet cut its 2027 hyperscaler and AI supply estimates.
GS US economists expect data centre moratoria to fade in importance and not be long-lived if enacted. GS believes its US datacentre forecasts to 2029 are 'appropriately conservative'.

Wilson's takeaway: the biggest issuers are likely ahead of themselves on funding, so financing supply will come in below current estimates. With lower rates and energy costs, a robust economy and labour market, and a GS forecast of 18% 2027 corporate EPS growth, he says don't write off 2026 continuing the 19/19 record of post-midterm equity rallies.

market_movers.rationale: NVDA realised 100 vol over the last 5 days. Wilson does not expect that to repeat in the next 5 days as exposures are reduced.
Apple, the largest index stock, is now negatively correlated with the Nasdaq, which complicates portfolio management.

sector_views.rationale: These 72 S&P names fell 13.3% in two days and trade at 13.1x NTM earnings, a 26% discount to the S&P. Wilson expects AI to be less dominant in the near term and volatility to fall.
The 5 hyperscalers rose 1.7% over two days and regained half the ground lost versus the S&P. Capex discipline could lift pricing for constrained compute.
They had their best month versus EuroStoxx on record, so the market has already rotated to safety.
Pressure through 2026 has yet to reverse, per the sub-sector YTD tables.

earnings_insights: GS forecasts 2027 corporate EPS growth of 18% (forecast, not a print).
NTM EPS estimates for the 72 AI spending beneficiaries are up more than 50% relative to the S&P 500 (estimate revisions, per GS Asset & Wealth Management).

macro_indicators.interpretation: Wilson cites robust payrolls and a strong labour market as support for equities despite the sell-off.
Worst 1-day equity performance since Apr 2025, according to GS credit strategists.
Regression implied 8.2bps, so credit is much more resilient than equity.
Cited as a support for a continued post-midterm rally.

trade_ideas.rationale: Credit spreads moved far less than regression implied on Thursday, and credit would underperform equity in a systematic risk-off. The pair keeps liquidity.

tension_points.bull_case: Payrolls were robust, positioning has been hit hard, rates and oil are easing, Democrats are unlikely to threaten aggregate growth, GS forecasts 18% 2027 EPS growth, and the 19/19 post-midterm rally record could continue. Wilson is in the 1997/1998 camp.
tension_points.bear_case: The sell-off in AI beneficiaries was extreme, the Democratic policy reaction function is unfamiliar, market structure is fragile, and credit's downside convexity has not kicked in. The last line of post-midterm gains looks tougher than it did on Wednesday.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Credit spreads widening as a systematic risk-off spreads from equity, or data centre moratoria that curb AI spending, would weaken the bull case.

tension_points.bull_case: Policy-driven supply discipline would raise pricing for constrained compute and lower capex, which favours hyperscalers with capacity. GS has not cut its 2027 estimates.
tension_points.bear_case: Hyperscaler issuance of $296b YTD is almost $50b above GS's assumption. The biggest issuers are likely ahead of themselves on funding, so financing supply may come in below current estimates.
